function: Channel estimation for uplink wideband XL-MIMO under near-field propagation, beam split and spatial non-stationarity, from hybrid-combined pilot observations (p. 1, p. 3-4).
system: Uplink TDD, hybrid BS with 4 RF chains, ULA 512 or UPA 2048 antennas, single-antenna users, OFDM 256 subcarriers at 100 GHz; no RIS (p. 3, p. 9).
method: Deep-unrolled proximal gradient descent, 5 layers, learnable step sizes and U-Net proximal networks; supervised L2 training with monotonic-descent constraint (primal-dual) and noise injection (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: near-field spherical-wave model with visibility-region masks, L=3 paths with random angles, distances, gains; 5x10^7 pairs per SNR, 70/10/20 split (p. 5, p. 9).
test_conditions: Train/test on same distribution per SNR (-5 to 10 dB); Fig. 8 tests models trained at L=3 or L=5 on other path numbers (p. 9, p. 11).
baselines: Classical: LMMSE, OMP with polar dictionary; learned: ISTA-Net+, AMP-SBL deep unrolling [46], D2-CNN (U-Net mapping signal to channel) (p. 9).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, pilot length, number of paths, unrolled layers and visibility model; FLOPs (p. 9-12).
complexity: Table I FLOPs (x10^9) on ULA: PGD-Net 3.79, D2-CNN 3.77, ISTA-Net+ 2.54, AMP-SBL 2.16, OMP 0.23, LMMSE 0.21 (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 5: "we establish channel models for two antenna configurations at the BS: uniform linear array and uniform planar array"; own simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 11: "PGD-Net (L = 3), where the network is trained only at L = 3 and evaluated at different path numbers"
q3_support: p. 9: "OMP: The orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm" (non-learned) and "AMP-SBL: A deep unrolling network combining approximate message passing and sparse Bayesian learning" (learned); NMSE compared in Fig. 6, p. 10
q4_support: p. 9: "Table I summarizes the computational complexity of the considered channel estimation benchmark, evaluated under the ULA configuration"; the table lists FLOPs, PGD-Net 3.79 x10^9
q5_support: p. 9: "The generated channel data are used to create data pairs"; data come from the paper's own simulator and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 2: the unrolled PGD network estimates the channel. q2 rests on Fig. 8 (trained at L=3 or L=5, evaluated at other path numbers); the subarray visibility test of Fig. 9 (p. 11-12) does not say whether the network was retrained, so it is not counted. No RIS in this paper.
